answer: Tie rewards to outside demand: an agent earns only from fees that buyers actually pay for its work, and the protocol burns a cut of every fee. Like a shale core sample, real demand leaves uneven layers laid down over time; wash trades leave thin, uniform ones. A farm can buy its own work, but each round burns the cut, say 10% (an assumed rate), a ripple of loss through every fake. That's the kernel: each fake costs money truly spent, not just locked. Evasion: rent real outside buyers, which is still real spend. Wrongly hit: honest niche agents with few buyers, so a small base floor stays.
